routes.name: Electronic Visitor Visa (e-Visa) for US, Canadian and Australian citizens
routes.summary: Since April 10, 2025, US, Canadian and Australian citizens need a visa to visit Brazil. The e-Visa is applied for 100% online through the VFS portal, for tourism, business, transit, or sports and artistic activities, up to 90 days.

other: Only for tourism, business, transit, and sports or artistic activities.
Holders of a valid traditional visa do not need an e-visa.
Other nationalities cannot use the e-Visa and apply for a regular visit visa (VIVIS).

sources.label: Brazilian Consulate in New York: e-Visa page
Brazilian Consulate in New York: visa fees

steps: Apply online on the VFS e-Visa portal
Upload documents and pay the fee

routes.name: Digital Nomad Visa and Residence (VITEM XIV, CNIg RN 45/2021)
routes.summary: Remote workers for a foreign employer can get a visa or in-country residence for up to one year. Renewable for an equal period. Working for a Brazilian employer does not qualify.

income.note: Foreign-source income. Alternative to the savings option.

savings.note: Bank funds, as an alternative to the income proof.

other: Must work remotely for a foreign employer or foreign clients. Not available to business owners.
Valid health insurance in Brazil is required for the consular visa application.
Criminal record certificate required (FBI check for US applicants).
Signed employer statement that the work can be done remotely, plus the applicant's own statement.

documents: Health insurance valid in Brazil (visa route)
Declaration of ability to work remotely
Contract or proof of link with the foreign employer
steps: Choose the consular visa route or the in-country residence route
Gather the digital nomad proof and criminal record documents

routes.name: Retiree or Pension Holder Residence (CNIg RN 40/2019)
routes.summary: Retirees or pensioners who will live in Brazil and transfer at least US$ 2,000 a month can get a temporary VITEM XIV visa.

income.note: Proof of monthly retirement income or pension.

other: Valid health insurance in Brazil required.
Criminal background check required (FBI check for US applicants).
Term and renewal rules not read on an official page.

routes.name: Work Residence Authorization (employer-sponsored, CNIg RN 2/2017 and others)
routes.summary: Immigrants who will work in Brazil apply for work residence through MigranteWeb, with a Federal Police step. Many specific categories exist (technical assistance, researchers, athletes, executives and more). Processing is up to 30 days for a properly filed case.

other: Category lists come from the Ministry of Justice resolutions index. Documents per category were not read.

routes.processing: The official page estimates up to 30 days if the case is correctly filed, and up to 60 days if extra documents are requested.
steps: File the residence request with documents and the paid GRU
Register with the Federal Police and get the CRNM card

sources.label: Ministry of Justice: list of CNIg normative resolutions

routes.name: Executive or Company Administrator Residence (CNIg RN 11/2017)
routes.summary: Directors and managers of a Brazilian company can get residence based on foreign direct investment. The 2024 update lists R$ 600,000 per executive, or R$ 150,000 with job creation. Needs review since only the amending text was read.

investment.note: Or R$ 150,000 with job creation, per the amending text.

other: Job creation requirement mentioned in the amending text (ten new jobs in two years). Base resolution RN 11 was not read.

routes.name: Individual Investor in a Brazilian Company (CNIg RN 13/2017)
routes.summary: Individuals can get temporary residence by investing at least R$ 500,000 in a Brazilian company, or R$ 150,000 in a Brazilian startup. The applicant's company files first in Brazil, then the consular visa follows.

investment.note: Brazilian company. R$ 150,000 minimum for a Brazilian startup.

other: Process starts in Brazil: the Brazilian company files with the Ministry of Justice, then the consulate issues the visa.

sources.label: Brazilian Consulate in New York: investor visa (VITEM IX)

routes.name: Real Estate Investor Residence (CNIg RN 36/2018)
routes.summary: Buy at least R$ 1,000,000 of urban real estate with foreign funds and get 4 years of residence, then an indefinite term if the investment stays. The minimum can be up to 30% lower in the North and Northeast.

investment.note: Urban real estate, can be split across properties. Up to 30% lower in the North and Northeast.

other: Funds must be personal and of foreign origin.
Must stay in Brazil at least 14 days in every two-year period.
Financing allowed only for the part above the minimum.
The consulate lists R$ 1,000,000 in the Center-West, Southeast and South, and R$ 700,000 in the North and Northeast.

stay.note: Can change to an indefinite term if the investment conditions are kept.

documents: Property registry certificate free of liens (built property)
Bank declaration confirming the international capital transfer
For property under construction: registered purchase promise contract, construction permit, incorporation memorandum

sources.label: Brazilian Consulate in New York: investor visa (VITEM IX)

routes.name: Study Residence Authorization
routes.summary: Study is one of the listed grounds for residence authorization with the Federal Police. Requirements and term were not confirmed.

other: Only the existence of this ground was confirmed. Documents and term not read.

routes.name: Family Reunification Residence
routes.summary: Family reunification is a listed ground for residence authorization with the Federal Police. Who qualifies and the documents were not confirmed.

other: Only the existence of this ground was confirmed. Eligible relatives and documents not read.

routes.name: Mercosur Residence Agreement
routes.summary: Citizens of Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru and Uruguay can get residence in Brazil under the Mercosur agreement. Separate rules exist for Venezuela, Suriname and Guyana nationals at the border.

other: Venezuelan, Surinamese and Guyanese nationals have a separate border-country residence ground where Mercosur does not apply.

routes.name: Humanitarian Residence and Protection
routes.summary: Brazil offers residence on humanitarian grounds, for example for Haitians, victims of trafficking, children traveling alone and people affected by the Syrian conflict. Refugee claims go through the official process.

other: Groups listed by the Federal Police include Haitians, stateless persons, trafficking victims, unaccompanied minors and people affected by the Syrian conflict.

routes.name: Indefinite-Term (Permanent) Residence
routes.summary: Temporary residence can be converted to an indefinite term through the residence authorization service. Years needed depend on the original ground and were not confirmed.

other: Years required by ground not confirmed on an official page.
Residence is lost after an absence of more than two years without justification (Decree 9,199, art. 135).
Residence card (CRNM) is valid for 9 years for indefinite-term holders (art. 74).

routes.name: Ordinary Naturalization
routes.summary: Ordinary naturalization needs 4 years of residence right before applying, Portuguese ability, and a clean criminal record. It drops to 1 year with a Brazilian child or spouse, or for people from Portuguese-speaking countries, and to 2 years for relevant service or professional merit.

eligibility.language: Able to communicate in Portuguese (level set by Ministry of Justice rules)
other: 4 years of residence right before the application. Trips abroad totaling over 12 months can block approval.
1 year if you have a Brazilian child, or a Brazilian spouse or partner you are not separated from.
2 years if you gave or can give relevant service to Brazil, or are recommended for professional, scientific or artistic ability.
1 year of uninterrupted residence plus good moral standing for people from Portuguese-speaking countries.
No criminal conviction, or rehabilitation. Apply at the Federal Police.
Extraordinary naturalization: more than 15 years of uninterrupted residence and no conviction, any nationality.

citizenship.note: Brazil does not ask you to give up your old nationality. Per Decree 9,199 art. 249, a Brazilian loses nationality only on acquiring another one in cases that are not exceptions (original nationality recognized abroad, or naturalization imposed by the foreign state). Years count from indefinite-term residence per art. 221. Decision deadline is 180 days.

routes.name: Naturalization for Stateless Persons
routes.summary: A recognized stateless person who chooses naturalization goes through a simplified process. They must show at least two years of residence in Brazil.

other: Must be recognized as stateless in Brazil.

routes.summary: Brazil has a gov.br service to get equal rights status for Portuguese citizens. Conditions were not read.
